HistoricalName: Calle de la Testa
EnglishName: Head Street
Description:
## Historical Background

Calle della Testa in Cannaregio, close to the Scuola Grande di San Marco, owes its name to the big sculpture of a head (testa) which can be found on a house in that ally. The street literally means "Street of the Head" in Italian.

## The Executioner's House

According to the tradition, the house which lodges this startling sculpture was home to one of the most active Serenissima executioners of the XV century. This reveals a grim aspect of Venice's judicial history during the Renaissance period.

## The Head's Sinister Fun

This means that the Venetian authorities would literally drop death warrants through this stone head to inform the executioner about upcoming executions - a macabre but efficient system of communication that maintained some distance between the state and its executioner.

This street and its sculptural head serve as a tangible reminder of Venice's complex history of justice and punishment during the Renaissance, when La Serenissima maintained strict order through sometimes harsh measures. The fact that this architectural detail has survived and given its name to an entire street shows how these darker aspects of history remain embedded in Venice's urban fabric.

EnglishName: Walkway of Saint Gerard Sagredo
Description: This area in the Cannaregio sestiere was known for its proximity to the Church of San Gerardo Sagredo, dedicated to the 11th-century Venetian saint. The fondamenta, or walkway, along the nearby canal was named after this church.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta de Santa Marta in Sestiere Dorsoduro
EnglishName: Quay of St. Martha in the Dorsoduro District
Description: Area near the Church of Santa Marta along the canal, part of the Dorsoduro sestiere. Known for shipping and maritime activities in the 15th century.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta degli Ognisanti
EnglishName: Foundations of All Saints
Description: This area in the Dorsoduro sestiere was known for its proximity to the Church of Ognissanti, a prominent religious landmark dedicated to All Saints. The fondamenta, or walkway along the canal, would have been a busy thoroughfare for locals and visitors alike.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta dei Narisi in Cannaregio
EnglishName: Wharf of the Narisi Family in Cannaregio
Description: A bustling area along a canal in the Cannaregio sestiere, known for its many artisan workshops and proximity to the Jewish Ghetto, which was established in 1516.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta dei Narisi, Sestiere Dorsoduro
EnglishName: Walkway of the Narisi Family, Dorsoduro District
Description: A walkway along a canal in the Dorsoduro district, likely named after a prominent local family. The area was known for its artisan workshops and proximity to the Zattere promenade.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta del Remèr in Sestiere Dorsoduro
EnglishName: Quay of the Oar Maker in Dorsoduro District
Description: This area, situated along the Rio de San Barnaba canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere, was known for its concentration of skilled artisans, particularly oar makers who crafted oars for Venice's many gondolas and boats.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta delle Zattere
EnglishName: Wharf of the Rafts
Description: This area along the Giudecca Canal in the sestiere of Dorsoduro was known for its zattere (rafts or barges) that would transport goods along the canal. The nearby Chiesa dello Spirito Santo church was a prominent landmark.

HistoricalName: Fondamenta San Severo, Sestiere Castello
EnglishName: San Severo Waterfront, Castello District
Description: The area was known for its proximity to the Church of San Severo and its location along the San Severo canal in the Castello sestiere, one of the six main districts of Venice.

HistoricalName: Ghetto Novo
EnglishName: New Ghetto
Description: Area of the Cannaregio sestiere where Jewish people were required to live under the Venetian Republic starting in 1516. It was one of the first Jewish ghettos in Europe.

HistoricalName: Ponte de le Maravegie, San Polo
EnglishName: Bridge of Wonders, San Polo
Description: A bridge in the San Polo sestiere, known for its artisan workshops and proximity to the Rialto market during the 15th century.

HistoricalName: Ponte dei Dai in Sestiere Cannaregio
EnglishName: Bridge of the Dai in Cannaregio District
Description: A bridge in the Cannaregio sestiere, near the Church of Santa Maria dei Miracoli. The area was known for its artisan workshops and proximity to the Jewish Ghetto.

HistoricalName: Ponte del Formager in Sestiere San Polo
EnglishName: Bridge of the Cheese Maker in the San Polo District
Description: This bridge was likely named after a nearby cheese maker or cheese market in the San Polo sestiere, one of the central districts of Venice known for its artisan shops and markets in the 15th century.

HistoricalName: Ramo del Figareto in Sestiere San Marco
EnglishName: Figareto Alley in the District of St. Mark
Description: A narrow alley located in the San Marco sestiere, known for its artisan workshops and proximity to Piazza San Marco, the political and religious heart of 15th century Venice.

HistoricalName: Ruga dei Oresi in Sestiere di Cannaregio
EnglishName: Goldsmith's Street in Cannaregio District
Description: This area in the Cannaregio sestiere was known for its concentration of goldsmiths and jewelers in the 15th century. It was situated near the Chiesa di Santa Sofia and the Rio di Santa Sofia canal.

HistoricalName: Sacca della Misericordia
EnglishName: Mercy's Sack
Description: In the 15th century, this area was a shallow lagoon used as a landfill and later filled in to create new land. It was not yet developed into the artificial island seen today.

HistoricalName: Sacca della Misericordia
EnglishName: Mercy's Shallows
Description: A shallow lagoon area in the Dorsoduro sestiere, known for its marshy wetlands and fishing activities during the 15th century.

HistoricalName: Salizada dei Greci
EnglishName: Way of the Greeks
Description: This area was historically known for its Greek immigrant population and the nearby Greek Orthodox church of San Giorgio dei Greci, founded in the late 15th century.

HistoricalName: Salizada San Pantalon in Sestiere di Santa Croce
EnglishName: San Pantalon Street in the District of Santa Croce
Description: This area was part of the Santa Croce sestiere, known for its artisan workshops and proximity to the Church of San Pantalon, which dates back to the 12th century.

HistoricalName: Salizada San Stae, Sestiere di Santa Croce
EnglishName: Salizada San Stae, District of Santa Croce
Description: This area was part of the Santa Croce sestiere, known for its artisan workshops and proximity to the Grand Canal. The nearby Chiesa di San Stae, a church dedicated to Saint Eustachius, dates back to the 11th century.

HistoricalName: Santa Chiara
EnglishName: Saint Clare
Description: In the 15th century, this area was likely known for the Chiesa di Santa Chiara, a church dedicated to Saint Clare that was located near the present-day Ponte della Libertà. The church was part of the Santa Croce sestiere.

HistoricalName: Sestiere di Dorsoduro, presso la Chiesa di San Sebastiano
EnglishName: Dorsoduro District, near the Church of San Sebastiano
Description: This area in the Dorsoduro sestiere was known for its proximity to the Church of San Sebastiano, which was consecrated in 1468 and housed paintings by renowned Renaissance artist Paolo Veronese.

HistoricalName: Strada de la Carità
EnglishName: Street of Charity
Description: This area was part of the Dorsoduro sestiere and was known for the presence of the Chiesa di Santa Maria della Carità, a church dedicated to the Virgin Mary of Charity. The church and its surrounding area were important religious and cultural centers in 15th century Venice.
